pages.text: Most processors have $(l)upgrade slots$() on the side of the GUI. Stack upgrade items in those slots to change behavior.$(br2)Slot 0 takes $(item)Energy Upgrades$(). Slot 1 takes speed-type upgrades. Single-slot processors take any speed-type.
$(item)Speed Upgrade$() adds $(l)+1 speed$() per item. Recipe runs faster, but $(c)energy cost grows quadratically$() with speed. Stack up to 64 per slot.
$(item)Energy Upgrade$() reduces energy cost (subtracts quadratically) and grows the internal energy buffer ($(l)x N / 10$()). Required to keep heavily speed-boosted processors affordable.
$(item)Stack Upgrade$() enables $(l)parallel processing$(): ceil(count / 4) recipes per tick, capped at 32. Acts like speed plus parallel I/O. More energy-efficient than raw speed.
$(item)Quantum Upgrade$() = $(l)x5 speed$() and $(l)1 parallel recipe per item$(). End-game tier. Energy cost scales hard. Pair with many Energy Upgrades.

pages.title: The Math
pages.text: $(l)speedMult$() = upgrades + 1 (x5 for quantum)$(br)$(l)parallel$() = ceil(stack / 4) or quantum count$(br)$(l)energyMult$() = max(speedMult, (speedMult - 1)^2 + speedMult - energyUp^2)$(br2)Energy upgrades cancel speed cost quadratically. Balance the two.

pages.title: GregTech Integration
pages.text: When GT energy cap is enabled, every $(l)N Energy Upgrades$() bumps the processor's accepted EU tier by $(l)+1$(). N comes from config $(o)ENERGY_UPGRADES_NEEDED_TO_NEXT_TIER$(). Hover the upgrade to see current N.
